PullRequest.Title: Chat: Plugins opens Customizations > Plugins in the editor window
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #348690

In the editor window, **Chat: Plugins** (and the `/plugins` slash command) opened the Extensions view filtered by `@agentPlugins`. That view only shows a welcome that sends you on to Chat Customizations, which costs an extra click. The Agents window already opened Customizations > Plugins directly.

## Change

`ManagePluginsAction.run` now always runs `aiCustomization.openManagementEditor` with the `plugins` section, so both windows behave the same. The `IWorkbenchEnvironmentService` and `IExtensionsWorkbenchService` dependencies are gone. The `@agentPlugins` Extensions filter and its welcome view are unchanged for anyone who types it.

## Testing

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/actions/chatPluginActions.test.ts --grep ManagePluginsAction`: the new test **fails without the fix** (actual `[["extensions.openSearch","@agentPlugins "]]`) and **passes with it**
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/actions/chatPluginActions.test.ts`: 49 passing
- `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/actions/chatPluginActions.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/actions/chatPluginActions.test.ts`: no problems
- UI scenario: run **Chat: Plugins** from the Command Palette, then expect the Customizations editor with **Plugins** selected. It fails on the current Insiders (the Extensions view shows `@agentPlugins`) and passes on a dev build of this branch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run Chat: Plugins or /plugins in the editor window with a local chat session, including first open and repeated invocation.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ManagePluginsAction awaits one OpenEditor command, which awaits editorService.openEditor before selecting Plugins. Editor construction/layout is synchronous; provider item loading, plugin filtering, and migration discovery are launched asynchronously and are not awaited by the action. Installed rows await provider data where applicable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate agents, skills, instructions, hooks and prompts through the prompts service; supplement skill metadata and expand hook files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached provider enumeration serves all five sidebar sections and plugin-count consumers. It launches five type-specific enumerations concurrently; underlying filesystem work scales with configured folders and customization files, not with the number of command dispatches while cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor-window command opened the Extensions container instead. This enumeration was reached upon separately opening Customizations; the same Customizations enumeration implementation and coalescing already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Async sidebar/item loading; not awaited by ManagePluginsAction or management-editor setInput.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check recovery-root existence, enumerate its directories, and read recovery manifests; potentially update interrupted migration status.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced refresh per initialization burst; absent root requires only one exists operation. Existing roots require one enumeration and sequential existence/read operations for each recovery directory, with status updates only for applicable running records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Not performed directly by the old Extensions-search command; the same discovery ran after a subsequent Customizations open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background discovery launched with void; does not block Plugins selection or command completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read legacy marketplace definitions from GitHub when the visible plugin home needs a marketplace snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only when legacy marketplace is available; one snapshot attempt per widget state, with loading, loaded and failed states suppressing repeated attempts. References are deduplicated by canonical ID. Cache misses resolve a ref and sequentially try the supported definition paths per GitHub repository; successful entries have an eight-hour cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: AgentPluginsListView.show already called fetchMarketplacePlugins for the @agentPlugins query without @installed. The PR changes the UI owner, not marketplace service fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Async snapshot population; command and installed-plugin UI do not await this network request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare marketplace repositories through clone/refresh fallback and read definition files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One preparation per effective clone-backed marketplace reference, not per plugin. Operations serialize per repository-operation key; different repositories may proceed concurrently. Refresh uses the existing eight-hour threshold; local references only check their directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old @agentPlugins query reached the same marketplace service and repository preparation behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of asynchronous legacy snapshot loading, off the action's completion path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Five fixed customization section types, configured customization folders/files, installed plugin count, deduplicated marketplace repository references, and migration recovery directories. User command frequency is explicit invocation, not input/scroll/render frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One nested command per invocation. Five local section queries share one provider promise. Initialization migration requests coalesce through a zero-delay Delayer. Marketplace references use Promise.all, while clone-backed operations are serialized per repository key, not globally.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Management input is singleton-style and selected-section dispatch returns early when already selected. Item sources cache an in-flight/resolved provider promise across section consumers and invalidate on provider changes. Plugin snapshots distinguish uninitialized/loading/loaded/failed, so empty or failed results are not retried on every render. GitHub success cache and repository refresh TTL are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in command routing, asynchronous loading, shared provider caching, snapshot lifecycle and repository-level grouping from implementation reads.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings or profiling are available. File counts, recovery history and marketplace configuration vary. Existing editor construction does additional work compared with displaying the former intermediary, but no pathological new multiplicity or blocking boundary was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: this is explicit navigation to the requested existing management UI. Existing initialization work is newly reachable directly, but the diff adds no per-item boundary amplification, retry loop, unbounded ownership, or awaited slow initialization. Marketplace work was already reachable from the old query.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run Chat: Plugins or /plugins in the editor window while an agent-host-backed customization harness is active.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command resolves the active harness/session, opens the same singleton management editor and then selects Plugins. Plugin rows asynchronously await shared provider customizations; migration information is independently deferred.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request runtime plugin installation inventory from the active backend target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inventory request per distinct runtime provider in the customization snapshot, concurrently via Promise.all; the shared PureItemProviderItemSource promise prevents one request per plugin or sidebar section.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old editor-window command opened Extensions search and did not assemble active-harness customizations directly. The same grouped inventories ran when Customizations was subsequently opened.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider customization assembly and populated plugin rows await inventories; editor opening/Plugins selection does not await them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Expand agent-host plugin directory contents through the filesystem provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold expansion scales with plugin directories and supported files; plugin expansions run concurrently. Warm expansion cache is keyed by plugin URI and validated by nonce and plugin label; all sidebar consumers share one provider enumeration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Not on the direct Extensions-search command path; the same cache-backed expansion occurred after opening Customizations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Async provider completion and row population; not awaited by the management-editor command.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover migration candidates and recovery manifests; query authoritative source folders for candidate types.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Coalesced initialization refresh; a fixed set of enabled migration categories runs concurrently. Source-folder queries are deduplicated by target prompt type rather than issued per candidate. Recovery manifests scale with recovery directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These existing migration checks were reached when the user proceeded from Extensions to Customizations, rather than by the initial Plugins command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the command completion path; migration results populate background UI.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct runtime providers, plugin directory contents, active-harness customization files, fixed migration categories and recovery history. Effective inventory cardinality is provider count, not installed plugin count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Inventories run concurrently across distinct providers, directory expansions across uncached plugins; all section reads coalesce into one provider call. Migration initialization is delayed/coalesced and uses cancellation/sequence checks. No new concurrency policy is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PureItemProviderItemSource caches the in-flight/resolved provider promise, invalidates on provider changes, and resets rejected promises. Directory expansions reuse nonce/label-validated entries. Repeated invocation reuses the singleton input; section selection has an unchanged early return.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in grouped inventory requests, provider-promise coalescing, expansion caching and the separation of async data population from command completion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host latency, plugin file counts and migration candidate counts are not measured. Broader initialization is the existing management UI's behavior, not evidence by itself of a newly pathological mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. The PR routes this explicit management workflow directly to an existing UI without defeating its caches or increasing its effective per-provider enumeration cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run Chat: Plugins or /plugins in the Agents window, including repeated opening and closing of Customizations.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Same as before: await OpenEditor, await editorService.openEditor, then select Plugins. Closing cancels migration refreshes, clears save handlers and disposes contributed-section widgets.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read grouped backend runtime plugin inventories during customization enumeration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per distinct runtime provider on a provider-cache miss, shared across section consumers; no change from base.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted isSessionsWindow branch already awaited the identical OpenEditor command with Plugins.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Async plugin population, not action completion; unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read uncached plugin directory contents and migration recovery data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cached per-plugin expansions and one coalesced recovery-discovery refresh, scaling with files/recovery directories; unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Async data population/background migration discovery; unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Conditionally load legacy marketplace definitions, including clone-backed fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One guarded snapshot per widget state and one service fetch per deduplicated reference on applicable cache misses; unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical management editor and marketplace cache/repository scheduling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Explicit user invocations, active provider count, plugin files, deduplicated marketplace references and recovery directories. The diff does not alter any of these multipliers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged grouped inventory concurrency, shared provider promise, per-repository clone sequencing and migration Delayer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Same singleton input, provider promise cache, expansion cache, marketplace snapshot states and service TTL as base. Existing migration cancellation and widget disposal remain intact.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the diff removes the window condition and retains the exact command and argument previously executed in this window.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No duration measurements; there is no changed work on this window's scenario to attribute to the PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the Agents-window call path is behaviorally unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over both changed files and every diff page against base 559eab763ec8cbba4eb10cd61df616cb43019f4b. Traced command palette/slash-command callers, old Extensions query, management-editor initialization/reuse/cleanup, grouped provider inventories, filesystem discovery, marketplace caches and per-repository sequencing. No actionable high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue or provenance-worthy performance regression fix established. Static read-only review; no runtime profiling.
